executionScenarios.name: happy-path
executionScenarios.description: Daily run fetches last-24h Exchange mail via HTTP Request, OpenAI extracts and prioritizes action items, and a structured digest email is sent.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: a daily Schedule trigger fires in the morning; Exchange/EWS credentials are assumed present on the HTTP Request node; OpenAI credentials assumed present. Runtime mocks: the HTTP Request node (reading the last 24h of Outlook/Exchange on-premise mail) returns 3 messages — (1) from 'jane@examplecorp.com', subject 'Contract renewal — needs sign-off by Friday', (2) from 'ops@examplecorp.com', subject 'Server migration window confirmed', (3) from 'newsletter@examplenews.com', subject 'Weekly digest'. The OpenAI node returns a structured JSON result with prioritized action items, e.g. [{ task: 'Sign contract renewal', priority: 'high', source: 'jane@examplecorp.com' }, { task: 'Acknowledge migration window', priority: 'medium', source: 'ops@examplecorp.com' }]. The digest-send call (HTTP Request / Microsoft node) returns a success response.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The workflow executes without errors. A Schedule trigger fires the run. The mail-fetch HTTP Request returns the 3 messages and feeds them into the OpenAI node. The OpenAI output (prioritized action items) is incorporated into the final digest email body, which references 'Contract renewal' and a high-priority item. The digest is sent via the send step exactly once.

executionScenarios.name: http-request-body-config-valid
executionScenarios.description: Load-bearing: the HTTP Request node used to read Exchange mail has a valid, internally consistent body configuration that passes validation.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: the freshly built workflow contains an HTTP Request node configured to fetch the last 24h of Outlook/Exchange on-premise mail (POST to an EWS/Exchange endpoint). Runtime mock: the endpoint returns a 200 with a list of 2 messages from 'jane@examplecorp.com' and 'ops@examplecorp.com'. This scenario specifically inspects the HTTP Request node's body parameters for consistency, then runs it.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The HTTP Request node's body configuration is internally consistent and valid: it is NOT in raw/specifyBody=raw mode while simultaneously carrying structured bodyParameters. If sendBody is true with specifyBody=raw, a single rawContentType is set and the body is a well-formed non-empty string; if structured parameters are used, specifyBody is json or form and every parameter is a well-formed name/value pair (no orphaned/empty body params). The node passes validation and the workflow executes without a submit-workflow or node-parameter validation error, completing the mail fetch.

executionScenarios.name: no-emails-in-window
executionScenarios.description: Edge: no messages arrived in the last 24h — the workflow handles the empty result gracefully.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: Preconditions: same scheduled daily build. Runtime mock: the mail-fetch HTTP Request returns an empty message list (zero items) for the last-24h window. OpenAI is given no action items to extract.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The workflow completes without errors. Either no digest is sent, or a digest is sent whose body clearly states there are no action items / no new mail for the period. The OpenAI and send steps do not throw on the empty input.
